passages.provision_quote: This bill would require a victim of the crime who wishes to be heard regarding the resentencing to notify the prosecution of their request for a hearing within 15 days of being notified that resentencing is being sought, and would require the court to provide an opportunity for the victim to be heard.
passages.note: Victim-notice/right-to-be-heard and parole-notice-cap bill; addresses victim procedure in resentencing/parole, not the punishment-vs-treatment severity axis the rungs order.

rows.reasoning: AB 88 gives crime victims notice and a right to be heard in resentencing proceedings and caps the notice victims must give to attend parole hearings at 15 days; it is her own act as author (enacted, approved by the Governor 2023-10-13, within her current term). This is a victim-procedure measure, not a statement on whether the system's response to lawbreaking should be 'support and treatment', 'real consequences', or 'the toughest penalties the law allows' -- it speaks to a different dimension of criminal justice than the one the rungs order, so it is adjacent/off-axis and cannot establish a chair.
needs_source: Her own words or a vote/sponsorship on a bill whose operative content sets sentencing severity, diversion, or treatment-vs-punishment policy for this ladder
